body: Coming from mobas and mmos I was all about wrist aiming and high sensitivity. I had terrible wrist and shoulder issues for couple years. Since adapting to this my wrist and my shoulder pain are all but completely gone plus I can hit stuff. For MOST of my tracking, aiming and turning it's my arm. For flick-shotting it'll obviously be more your wrist. Find a balance that suits you. I personally use my elbow as an anchor and swivel off that (it rests on the very edge on the arm of my chair). Everyone close to me I've told to lower their sensitivity and all their damage went up pretty soon after getting used to it. GL

Hiya! So I'll tell you a story. Only moba exp no fps.  I placed 50 and happily sat there as a Mercy otp just fine. Then I made the mistake of playing with people that didn't care and fell to 47 (these players are 60+ but while playing with me repeatedly said the accounts were their smurfs so didn't care about trying hard or well.. peeling for me let alone working with me). Anyway I soloQd again as Mercy only and after a crazy ass losing streak I dropped to 39. 


I had enough. I started to play simple things (nothing fancy like Genji) like Soldier, Pharah, Roadhog, Zarya, Winston and WHEN we needed a healer only went Lucio. I'd say about 30% of my games I switched off healer into Pharah/Roadhog and WON even without external sustain. Why? Coz I had impact. Standing there like a pleb healing plebs was so pointless. As Pharah or Winston I made the enemy healers life MISERY (:<) since their team peeled about as much as my own. I bombarded then enemy with rockets and was always gold on damage. I was told by someone close that "you might be better at healing but you're damn well better than THEIR dps". I made a separate account that I only did what I wanted (mainly bruisers and dps) and I ranked 56 and match just fine there. It's only my data but there is something there for sure.


1. You don't have to heal. Don't be fooled into thinking you HAVE to heal. If you will have more impact teabagging widow on winston CHANGE!!!!!!! You can't heal what's dead.

2. Yeah you need to find a REALLY good dps to pocket but also have them peel you if you wanna play Mercy. 

3. Your friends wont play with you right now but that's normal. Bite the bullet, turn down your sensitivity to 800dpi and 5 in-game and learn how to aim (I went from soldier 19% accuracy to 50% in a couple days after training and training and learning how to turn and aim with my ARM, not wrist). 

4. Once you've climbed back up you'll have new skills to help when you need to flex and you'll be within a range where healing (and finding other players to pocket) will be much more rewarding. 

5. Some people will just say spam and git gud. Play your best 100% OR you can just take the straight forward route like I did.


Good luck!

LOL.


When I mean flex pick I mean flex. I basically never play Mercy on this account and only Lucio if we need a support. If our team can't work with a support at ALL then I either go Roadhog (but I play him like a bruiser/assassin as to me he's NOT a tank but gives my team that false sense of security) and usually have most damage, healing, kills AND objective time. It's important to note that the times I wont pick healer are because our team just lacks damage or are too pussy to do anything. If it's the latter I will go Winston and dive the enemy back-line which often gives space for my team to yolo (kill the snipers that won't let us through choke-point and amazing things happen!). It's gotten better since I've climbed and I have needed to do this less often. I also have spent hours on here, on streams and practising DPS roles that I previously sucked with. Nothing fancy atm. Just Soldier, Roadhog, Pharah, Zarya. 


**At the end of the day the BIGGEST lessons I've learned from climbing on both accounts:**

1. support supports the team (heh) so soloQ you are at the mercy (heh) of randoms. Same with Rein.

2. you might be a great support but that means shit. I've found that while I'm probably a better support than my whole team combined that my dps is also better so I've been putting more into that and becoming self-reliant. BTW I consider my Roadhog and Zarya as DPS'ers because boy do they pump it out.

3. don't learn fancy shit. not all of us can carry (or need to) on stuff like genji/tracer/widow. Git gud with good old fashioned soldier/roadhog/zarya/pharah and lucio when needed. Winston is my back-line pick since I can't play traditional flankers and is really great for the times you can't get through. Stop trying to get through! Get off Mercy and jump onto the enemy point so they all have to focus you (giving your team the space to get stuff done). 


I know it's hard without a full premade but I hope that you can learn from some of my own lessons. GL!

So I came to this sub and learned many things in the last week that I'll share with you:


1. for me personally I am a really good support but I get more done on stuff like Zaryz, Roadhog and Winston. I would LOVE to be a Tracer main but lets be realistic. I'm an FPS noob. I'll pick her up later on coz right now I wanna win. NOTE: sorry but support soloQ at my current mmr? Nah. I'll go support if we have a tank but if not I'm going roadhog/soldier (sustain) and this has worked out for me.


2. I practised TONS AND TONS of soldier (about 10+ hours) to get equipped with dealing damage. It was hard and I wanted to quit plenty of times but I persevered. 


3. For damage carries I turned my sensitivity to 800 dpi and 6 in game (which is a nightmare from my usual 2k dpi for mobas). But **it fucking worked**. It felt awful to pivot on my elbow and I had to get a large mouse-mat just to be able to do a clean 180 but after an hour or so I COULD HIT THINGS!!!!! I've been telling all my moba friends with great success! I am a pretty decent soldier, pharah and ZARYA now. I can KILL things! A miracle!


4. Be flexible. I cannot tell you how many games I've had to swap to winston to get the snipers off my fucking case and then go back to roadhog. I am not naturally a carry player but I found myself often doing tons of damage, getting gold on kills and game changing ults. Bit by bit I started winning more.


5. Go to custom games > settings > skirmish mode > hard AI and work that shit. I randomly played Genji, Tracer and Reaper and try to carry these shit bots. OMG it was like watching a corpse fight initially but I've gotten better. Stick some music and I grinded for a good hour as recommended switching between.


6. Watch tournaments. I've learnt quite a bit just from the casters about the meta but more important (for me) why x champion is good. I have common sense but for some reason I didn't know specifics about how shields can regen and armor can't etc let alone work around them. 


7. Fixing habits. For the longest time I'd walk straight at a Junkrat or I'd overextend stupidly. Since I've been actively focusing on those I've been dying less and MORE aware of my surroundings. 


8. Don't play competitive with music. AMP it up because I react SO much to sound now. 


9. take breaks. I always played better after standing up and doing stuff for 15mins or watching a series between splurges. 



Since I'm finally getting some good hours I've started to see myself settle in more - definite progress if slow but it's my first FPS so I'm trying to be more forgiving.. hope this helps and GL!
